# F1: Keyboard shortcut to open task details
<!-- packet-artifact-id:v1 {"uid":"6e7690d6-d10c-499c-a804-f8564cbbf0ec","displayId":"F1","title":"Keyboard shortcut to open task details"} -->
<!-- packet-change:v1 {"schemaVersion":1,"uid":"6e7690d6-d10c-499c-a804-f8564cbbf0ec","displayId":"F1","status":"ready"} -->

**Status:** Ready

## Intent
Operators spend most time driving the Kanban with a mouse; reaching for the trackpad to open an implementation task's details interrupts review flow. A single-keypress affordance restores keyboard continuity without competing with the many future shortcuts the app will accrue.

## Current Behavior
In `src/ui/layout.rs::paint_tasks`, clicking an implementation-task card's title sets the `packet_selected_task` temporary, which causes `paint_tasks` to invoke `overlays::show_panel_modal` titled "<Task #NNN> / Task details". There is no keyboard path. The codebase contains no `KeyCode` bindings, no global input-dispatcher module, and no documented accelerators — every interaction today is a mouse-clicked egui widget.

## Desired Behavior
With focus outside a text-edit or a chat-composer box, pressing the shortcut opens the details modal for:
1. The hovered implementation-task card, if the pointer is over one; otherwise
2. The previously selected implementation task (`packet_selected_task` temporary).
Planning-card cards, setup-attention cards, and the batch README cards are intentionally excluded — this shortcut scopes to implementation-task cards only (consistent with the 'open task details' phrasing in product copy). Pressing the shortcut again, or closing the modal, returns to the board unchanged. No new persistent UI state.

## Scope
- In: introduce a minimal egui `Input::event` listener bound to the chosen chord(s); wire the resulting action to the same temporary-slot path used by the existing card-title click; disable the chord while any editable egui widget consumes input (egui's existing `edit_focus` mechanism).
- Out: a general-purpose keyboard-navigation system (arrow-key card traversal, modal hotkeys, configurable binding editor, on-screen hints UI).
- Out: covering planning-item cards, planning-work cards, setup-attention cards, archived cards, or the Batch README cards.
- Out: multi-window or per-project shortcut customization.

## Affected Product Areas
- Board interaction (Kanban card selection)
- Application input handling (first keystroke dispatcher for the app)
- Task-details modal open/close semantics

## Requirements
1. With the board visible and no editable widget focused, pressing the primary chord (R1) opens the details modal for the hovered implementation-task card. The modal shows identical content to the mouse-click path.
2. If no card is hovered, the chord opens the details for the last-selected implementation task when one exists (R2).
3. While an editable widget (`TextEdit` or chat composer) has focus, the chord does not fire and passes through to normal editing behavior (R3).
4. Opening the modal does not disturb scroll position, tab selection, chat-tab state, or the current chat draft (R4).
5. Closing the modal preserves whatever `packet_selected_task` held before the chord fired, so subsequent chord presses reopen the same task (R5).
6. The chord is inert on the Welcome/connect screen and while any settings/import/MCP modal overlays the workspace (R6).
7. The shortcut is discoverable: the details-panel header includes the chord on hover text of the existing card title button ('Open task details \(Alt+D\)'), consistent with the surrounding `on_hover_text` conventions (R7).

## Decisions and Assumptions
- Shortcut convention (Delegated Agent choice, reversible): **Primary: Alt+D**. Fallback platform mapping: macOS ⌥+D; Linux Alt+D; Windows Alt+D. Rationale from repository evidence: (a) the codebase has zero prior accelerators, so no collision to honor — the choice defines the first convention the rest of the app will extend; (b) Alt-as-primary-alternator is the desktop-native accelerator prefix on both GNOME/KDE and Windows for feature-invoking chords (e.g., Alt+F File menu family), avoiding the modifier-heavy Space/Shift territory reserved for scrolling or typing; (c) 'D' is the shortest semantic vowel consonant for 'Details'; (d) egui's `Input::event()` will deliver the raw `(modifiers, Key)` pair cleanly regardless of platform remapping. Recorded as Assumption (Agent authority) and intentionally left reversible — if a downstream collision emerges in a future feature (say a debug toggle wanting Alt+D), the swap cost is confined to a single constant in the new dispatcher and one hover-text string.
- Scope limited to implementation-task cards, matching the standing policy that 'open task details' refers specifically to implementation-task cards; planning-specification cards remain a separate surface. This narrows the modal-invocation path to one temporary (`packet_selected_task`) and excludes the planning-selection temporary (`packet_selected_planning`) entirely.
- No new configuration file, no persistence, no onboarding tooltip. The chord is fixed for v1; a configurability requirement can land as a follow-up feature.
- No ADR warranted: single-user-facing convenience choice, fully invertible at a single constant, not a durable architectural commitment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Hovering a task card on the Ready board and pressing the chord opens '<Task #NNN> / Task details'. Content matches the equivalent mouse click pixel-for-pixel. Reproducible on the current project (fixture task #003 and #002 both qualify).
- AC2: With no hover and task #002 previously selected, pressing the chord reopens the #002 details.
- AC3: Typing 'd' with Alt held inside the chat composer or the '+ New Task' draft text field inserts the character as-is; no modal opens.
- AC4: After opening via chord, Esc closes the modal and `packet_selected_task` retains its pre-chord value; pressing the chord twice more reopens the same task.
- AC5: Alt+D produces no effect on the Welcome screen, while the Workspace→Settings… modal is up, or while the Import/MCP modal is up.
- AC6: Regression: clicking a task card title still opens details, the existing card-title hover-tooltip is now suffixed with '\(Alt+D\)', and no other behavior in `paint_tasks` or `task_details::paint` changes.
